text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with LLMs through prompts, and good prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions, can greatly improve the results. These models are capable of writing texts, translating languages and answering questions. However, they also have limits: they can make mistakes, produce false information, and they only know what their training data contains.
